gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced a net strengthening of prior year reserves by $13.653 million in 2021, representing a 1.27% increase relative to opening gross claims outstanding. This strengthening primarily impacted 2018 and prior years of account, specifically in Professional Indemnity, Management & Transactional Liability, Contractors liability, and Hull classes, indicating adverse claims development likely influenced by social and economic inflation trends. The combined ratio was negatively impacted by this strengthening. The year also saw significant natural catastrophe events including Hurricane Ida, Windstorm Uri, and the German Floods.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1274 opened 2021 with gross claims outstanding of $1,078.4m. During 2021 the Syndicate recorded adverse prior-year development, with a net deterioration of $13.65m (1.27% of opening gross claims), driven by adverse claims development and reserve strengthening on older years (notably 2018 and earlier) primarily in professional indemnity, management & transactional liability, contractors liability and hull. COVID-19 continued to have an adverse impact (reported $29m in the prior year), and 2021 natural catastrophe activity (Hurricane Ida, Windstorm Uri, German Floods) also affected the year. The movements are described in the technical reserves notes and related commentary.
